question: Give feedback on this drawing at the colour entrance. File: evals/files/scribble.png
ground_truth: Two to four short sentences naming the orange looping lines and the green dots, praising the movement or the choice rather than the child, ending with one open question about what is happening in the picture. No evaluative adjectives, no guess about what the loops represent, no correction.
expected_behavior: Opens with I see or I notice
Names at least two details visible in the drawing
Praises an action or a choice, never a trait
Ends with one open question about the world inside the picture
Keeps every sentence short

expected_behavior: Names the purple shape, the sun and the two figures

question: Give feedback on this drawing at the colour entrance. File: evals/files/cat-shaded.png
ground_truth: Acknowledges the shading and the trees drawn smaller to sit further away, as effort toward depth, without correcting proportions or judging realism. On the colour entrance the drawing is never corrected, however observational it looks.
expected_behavior: Notices the shading and the size difference between the trees
Acknowledges effort toward depth without correcting it
Does not use the words realistic or lifelike as a standard

question: Give feedback on this drawing at the sketch entrance. File: evals/files/sphere-study.png
ground_truth: A technical read of a shaded sphere: names where the light turns on the form and where the cast shadow sits, gives any slip in tone or proportion as something to try rather than something wrong, invents no story about the sphere, and ends with one open question about the student's own process.
expected_behavior: Opens with a plain observation about the light, the proportion or the structure
Names at least two things visible in the drawing, such as the cast shadow or the highlight
Gives a correction as something to try, never as something got wrong
Invents no story about the sphere
Ends with one open question about the student's own process

question: Give feedback on this drawing at the sketch entrance. File: evals/files/blank-page.png
ground_truth: The same blank page as negative-blank-page, at the other entrance. Measured: the sketch line described it as a shaded figure study with shoulder proportions and 暗部留白, none of which exists. The blank-page refusal was in the shared tail and was reached only after a prompt that had already told the model it was looking at an observational drawing and must read the light. A refusal that only holds at one entrance is not a refusal.
expected_behavior: Says the page looks blank and asks for another photograph
Names no light, no proportion, no structure and no tone
Invents no figure, no plaster cast and no still life
Does not open with a technical observation about a drawing that is not there

question: Give feedback on this drawing at the colour entrance. File: evals/files/local/savanna-acrylic.jpg
ground_truth: A real acrylic painting by a child: a spotted big cat walking left, a giraffe reaching into a tree, a zebra in front of it, a low yellow sun and an ochre ground. The reply names things that are actually on the paper, asks what is happening between the animals, and does not decide which animal is which species beyond what the marks support. The first real drawing in this suite; everything else is generated, and a generated fixture cannot fail the way a busy painting can. Skipped when the local file is absent.
expected_behavior: Names at least two things genuinely visible: the spots, the stripes, the tree, the sun
Does not assert a species the marks do not settle, and does not correct the animals
Asks one open question about what is happening between them, not about what was drawn
Uses no praise words and does not rank the work
Stays short enough for a child to hold in their head

question: Give feedback on this drawing at the sketch entrance. File: evals/files/local/geometry-three-solids.png
ground_truth: A real graphite study of a cube, a sphere and a cylinder under one light, with cast shadows falling to the right. The reply reads the light and the form, offers at most one thing to try rather than one thing done wrong, invents no story about the solids, and ends with a question about the student's own process. Skipped when the local file is absent.
expected_behavior: Opens on the light, the proportion or the structure rather than on liking it
Names at least two visible things, such as the cast shadows or the tone on the cylinder
Gives at most one correction, and gives it as something to try
Invents no story about the solids
Ends with one open question about how the student worked
